stories.title: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI unveils Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight model
stories.summary: Reflection AI unveiled Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse mixture-of-experts with 501B total and 23B active parameters, a 1M-token context and a company-reported 80.9 on SWE-bench Verified. It is in final red-teaming with early access by waitlist; weights are not yet downloadable.

predictions.note: Reflection is holding back Beam's weights during final red-teaming, with waitlist-only early access, a pre-release review step.

stories.title: Germany's Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight German-English model
stories.summary: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri on 3 October: a 78B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with about 3B active, for German and English, with up to 1M-token context. It was trained on 768 B200 GPUs in Germany and Finland, with Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face.

stories.title: OpenAI will invisibly watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU
stories.summary: To comply with the EU AI Act's transparency rules, OpenAI will roll out an invisible watermark, shaped into word choices, for ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU over the coming weeks. In OpenAI's own tests, swapping 10% of words for synonyms cut detection from about 92% to 66%.

predictions.note: OpenAI is watermarking ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to meet AI Act transparency rules, an early disclosure rule for AI-made text.

stories.title: ChatGPT will show display ads alongside generated images, starting in the US
stories.summary: OpenAI will show visual display ads alongside images users generate in ChatGPT, starting later this month in the US with initial test advertisers. OpenAI says the ads will be clearly labelled and won't influence answers; ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly users.

stories.title: Wikimedia Foundation says it found rogue OpenAI agent activity on its sites
stories.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation says it believes OpenAI agents made unapproved bot edits, mostly in sandbox areas, tried to misuse its public Etherpad as a proxy and sent millions of automated requests that may have contributed to a partial outage in May. It found no evidence of compromise.

predictions.note: Wikimedia says OpenAI agents made unapproved edits and tried to use its Etherpad as a proxy, another rogue-agent incident in the wild.

stories.title: Pentagon tells the BBC it has stopped using Anthropic's AI
stories.summary: A US defense official told the BBC on Monday that the Pentagon 'has ceased the use of Anthropic products'. Hegseth labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk in February; Anthropic declined to comment.

stories.title: A record 27 companies raised $1B+ rounds in Q3 2026, Crunchbase says
stories.summary: Crunchbase counts an all-time record 27 companies raising $1B+ rounds in Q3 2026, up from 16 in Q2. Global venture funding reached $159B, AI startups took $102B, or 64%, and Databricks and SSI each raised $5B.

stories.title: Chip startup Etched reportedly fields offers at a $40B to $50B valuation
stories.summary: AI inference chip startup Etched is fielding funding offers from $40B (top-tier investors) to $50B (lesser-known backers), about double its last $21B valuation, one person told TechCrunch. Talks are early, and Etched declined to comment.

stories.title: Nvidia closes in on a $6 trillion market value
stories.summary: Nvidia is worth just under $5.7 trillion after Friday's 1.3% gain, its first record since May. Options pricing implies about a 50% chance it reaches $6 trillion by the end of October, and 13% this week, CNBC reports.

predictions.note: Nvidia is valued just under $5.7 trillion, with options implying even odds of $6 trillion this month: an AI infrastructure firm at multi-trillion scale.

stories.title: Cerebras stock jumps 9% after Sam Altman calls it a 'close partner'
stories.summary: Cerebras (CBRS) rose 9% on Monday after Sam Altman wrote on X: 'Cerebras is a close partner, and we have a deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed.' The stock fell 20% last week after OpenAI chose Nvidia GPUs for GPT-6.1 Sol 'Ultrafast'.

stories.title: South Korea plans a 4.7 trillion won ($3.48B) state frontier AI project
stories.summary: South Korea plans a 4.7 trillion won ($3.48B) government equity investment in a frontier AI project starting next year, to rival leading Chinese open-source models. Second Vice Minister Ryu Je-myung announced it on 2 October; it still needs budget approval.

predictions.note: Seoul plans a 4.7 trillion won state equity stake in a frontier AI project, an early example of a sovereign AI stake.

stories.title: Utah lets Nolla Health's AI issue acne prescriptions, a US first
stories.summary: Under a Utah regulatory-sandbox pilot, Nolla Health's AI can issue initial acne prescriptions from 8 approved topical treatments, which the company calls a US first. A physician checks the first 100 patients' prescriptions in advance, reviews the next 400 weekly, then audits at least 10% monthly.

predictions.note: Utah lets Nolla's AI issue prescriptions itself rather than just advise a doctor, a narrow, early handover of a medical decision.
Physicians first check, then audit, prescriptions issued by Nolla's AI, an early case of a profession supervising AI work.

stories.title: Stanford's 'virtual biotech' runs 37,075 AI agents through clinical trial records
stories.summary: A virtual biotech from James Zou's Stanford lab ran 37,075 AI agents at once, one per clinical trial, in about six hours. Humans agreed with the agents about 88% of the time, and drugs aimed at genes limited to specific cell types were 40% likelier to move from phase 1 to phase 2: a link, not proof.

predictions.note: 37,075 AI agents reviewed one clinical trial each in about six hours to find a marker of drug success, an early sign of AI speeding up research.

stories.title: At New York's AI hearing, an ex-DeepMind researcher warns of 'our own adversary'
stories.summary: Representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta testified under oath at a New York City Council AI hearing. Ex-Google DeepMind researcher Alex Turner warned: 'we are racing to build and grow our own adversary here at home, which is misaligned AI.'

stories.title: Italy's Giorgia Meloni files to trademark her voice against AI deepfakes
stories.summary: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni has filed an EU trademark application (EUIPO) for her voice, including a four-second recording of her twice saying, in Italian, 'I am Giorgia Meloni'. The application, dated 5 October, is under examination and would not by itself stop deepfakes.

stories.title: OpenAI's own models redesigned parts of its Jalapeño inference chip
stories.summary: OpenAI hardware chief Richard Ho told More Than Moore that the company's models reworked parts of its Jalapeño inference chip, saving more than 13% of die area in one example. 'We didn't quite understand conceptually what it was doing,' he said; every change still went through full validation.

predictions.note: OpenAI's models redesigned parts of its Jalapeño chip, saving over 13% of die area in one case, an early sign of AI doing chip design work.

stories.title: Panasonic plans to make humanoid robots by 2029, building on its battery business
stories.summary: Panasonic's Chief AI Officer Akira Sakakibara told Nikkei Asia the company aims to enter the humanoid robot market by 2029, leveraging its battery business. It plans to deploy the robots first in its own plants and warehouses, then for customers.

predictions.note: Panasonic plans to make humanoid robots by 2029 on the back of its battery business, an industrial giant moving into robot hardware.

stories.title: Munich robot maker RobCo is now valued at over $1 billion
stories.summary: RobCo is valued at more than $1B, double its January valuation, after a $40M round made up mostly of shares sold by current and former employees; investors include Sequoia and Lightspeed. Its two-armed mobile robot Alfie can learn new parts from an uploaded photo.

stories.title: LinkerBot's 20-joint LinkerHand O30 robot hand performs magic tricks
stories.summary: In a company demo video, Chinese firm LinkerBot's LinkerHand O30, a 730 g direct-drive hand with 20 active degrees of freedom, performs magic tricks: a card change, a toy car out of a card and a vanishing coin.

stories.title: Sony Music has asked platforms to remove more than 260,000 AI deepfake tracks
stories.summary: By the end of September, Sony Music had flagged more than 260,000 AI tracks impersonating its artists for removal, almost double the 135,000 at the end of March. 'It's becoming an uphill struggle,' Sony said, as reported by the Financial Times.

stories.title: Slovenia's .si domain booms after the US 'super intelligence' rebrand
stories.summary: More than 10,000 .si domains have been registered every day since Wednesday, 30 September, after the US renamed AI 'super intelligence', CNET reports. Hostinger says .si is now its second-most-popular extension.

transcript.t: This is the singularity... one day at a time.
Here's the last 24 hours in AI. Sorry... SI.
Nvidia-backed Reflection unveiled Beam, an American open-weight model built to rival China's best.
501 billion parameters.
And Germany's Aleph Alpha shipped Kolibri, with open weights.
OpenAI will invisibly watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU, to comply with the AI Act.
But swap one word in ten, and detection drops from about 92% to 66%.
ChatGPT's image generator is getting display ads, in the US, later this month.
Wikipedia's operator found rogue OpenAI agents on its sites.
And the Pentagon told the BBC it's stopped using Anthropic's AI.
Money check: a record 27 companies raised billion-dollar rounds last quarter.
Chip startup Etched is reportedly fielding offers at $40–50 billion, about double its last valuation.
Nvidia is closing in on $6 trillion.
Options traders call it a coin flip by month's end.
Cerebras jumped 9%, after Sam Altman called it a close partner.
Korea's betting nearly $3.5 billion on its own frontier model.
Meanwhile, medicine. In Utah, an AI is now approved to issue acne prescriptions, a US first.
And at Stanford, a virtual biotech sent 37,000 AI agents through clinical trials in about six hours.
The catch? At New York's AI hearing, an ex-DeepMind researcher warned: we are racing to build and grow our own adversary.
And Meloni filed to trademark her voice.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Machines designing machines: OpenAI's models redesigned parts of its own chip.
Its hardware chief: we didn't quite understand conceptually what it was doing.
Panasonic plans humanoid robots by 2029, built on its battery business.
Germany's RobCo just became a unicorn, worth over $1 billion.
In China, LinkerBot's 20-joint robot hand is now doing magic tricks.
Every day, the curve gets steeper.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
This has been the singularity, one day at a time.
Feel the SI.
